newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover eases in week to Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover eases in week to Jan 31.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday reported a 0.45 percent decline in turnover in the week ending January 31.
Total BSE turnover stood at 33.701 million dinars ($6.227 million) in 159 transactions, down from 33.852 million dinars and 156 transactions a week ago.
"The market seems to be back to normal with weekly turnover exceeding 30 million dinars and supply and demand fairly balanced," a trader said.

Turnover sharply fell at the beginning of January when the dinar black market rate tumbled to 4.3 to the German mark during thed first days of 1997, prompting a flight of capital from the official financial market.
The central bank announced measures limiting credit activity of insolvent commercial banks and the rate soon returned to 3.8.
Traders said continuing political turmoil in Belgrade had not affected the market which reacted primarily to the poor liquidity in the banking sector.
For the week ending January 31, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 124 times for a volume of 16.15 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 22 transactions totalling 2.79 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 793 percent.
* BSE reported seven deals in the central bank short-term bonds worth 5.31 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper, treasury bills and certificates of deposit almost doubled to stand at 38.238 million dinars, up on 19.241 million a week ago.

* OTC trade in giro money market segment, where banks trade their surplus liquidity, jumped to 35.592 million dinars from 25.56 million a week ago. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
